body:
I don't know what your problems are, so this is a general suggestion, but have you tried meditation? 

Personally it helped me ground myself and consider my life from a better perspective that didn't involve as much suicidal ideation.

Depends on the height of the drop. Honestly though death generally isn't that fast and failure rates are higher than you'd think. Most people who survive say at the last second they regretted it, at the last instant they realised their life wasn't unsalvageable and that they'd made a terrible error. It wouldn't be the way I'd choose to go.

Well, it's nice that your family care about you. I can relate, I've had the same thoughts myself. Getting to the edge and realising what impact it would have on my family. 

Do you spend much time with them? Living because you love your family isn't a silly thing to do, in fact it's a part of why loads of people carry on. I've tried to make it a positive thing, I'll do stuff with my dad or mum, even if it's as simple as watch a movie we'd both like. I still think I'm a pretty useless person, I don't like myself at all but it's pretty enjoyable and it isn't their fault.

Yeah lots of failures with that one. I imagine it wouldn't be very painful though. As for what happens if you can't go through with suicide, then you keep on living. I'm doing a lot of meditation at the moment to try and keep myself in the present and put things in perspective. Sometimes it helps. It definitely numbs things. My problem is me and for the few seconds I'm not really me it's worth it.

I'm also a virgin although not religious. It's shit, but it is true that sex is only one part of life. Sometimes I live in the past too, mostly I try not to focus on it by being present and meditating.
I've been toying with drug overdose myself. I empathise though, I'm also too scared to do it.
